methodology.method_family: systematic compilation and synthesis of indicators and online knowledge systems
methodology.study_design: review compiling 145 operational marine biodiversity indicators and examining 223 marine-relevant online knowledge systems active in December 2025
methodology.sample_description: operational marine biodiversity indicators and marine-relevant online biodiversity knowledge systems
methodology.sector: marine biodiversity monitoring and ocean environmental governance
methodology.technology_context: marine biodiversity indicators, online biodiversity knowledge systems, generic AI and machine-learning for underwater imagery and environmental DNA processing

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The document is a marine biodiversity indicator and online knowledge-system review. It does not address LLMs, conversational AI, chatbots, agents, RAG, or governance of generative AI in regulated settings.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text contains governance, accountability, transparency, monitoring, and generic artificial intelligence terms, these refer to ocean biodiversity policy reporting and environmental observation systems, not to conversational governance of LLM-based systems. AI is mentioned only as support for imagery and e-DNA processing in marine monitoring.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit in title, abstract, and methods; no ambiguous overlap with conversational LLM governance.

appraisal.notes: Methodological appraisal reflects the marine biodiversity review itself. Transferability to the target review on conversational governance of LLMs is very low despite surface keyword overlap from Python triage.

cerqual.explanation: Within its own domain the review appears coherent and adequately described, but relevance to LLM conversational governance in regulated environments is negligible because the study object is marine biodiversity indicators and online knowledge systems.

coding.theme: Marine biodiversity monitoring and indicator governance
coding.subtheme: Online biodiversity knowledge systems for policy reporting

synthesis.main_claim: Existing marine biodiversity indicators and online knowledge systems were systematically compiled and assessed for alignment with monitoring needs, data readiness, analytical maturity, and policy reporting pipelines.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a broad marine-focused evaluation of 145 indicators and 223 online systems using an SPRB framework to support ocean governance and decision-making.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence on conversational LLM governance; at most marginal foundational context only if the review broadens to generic environmental data-governance infrastructures, which is outside current scope.

evidence.claim: Online systems enable interaction with biodiversity data, not conversational AI

evidence.claim: Trusted data governance concerns biodiversity knowledge systems
evidence.excerpt: System endurance and analytical value are shaped by user focus, indicator transparency, update cadence, and trusted data governance

evidence.claim: SPRB framework used to classify indicators and systems
evidence.excerpt: We used the State-Pressure-Response-Benefit (SPRB) framework to categorise both marine biodiversity indicators and online biodiversity knowledge systems
